name: Potassium tantalate
equilibrium_context: Quantum paraelectric, no ferroelectricity down to absolute zero
summary: Control and negative entry on the SrTiO3 controversy.

driven_states.emergent_property: Intense THz excitation of the soft mode produces a long-lived second-harmonic response which, however, does not stem from a global ferroelectric phase but from a THz-driven correlation between defect-induced local polar structures.
driven_states.source: Cheng, Kramer, Shen & Hoffmann, Phys. Rev. Lett. 130, 126902 (2023), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.130.126902
driven_states.caveat: Deliberately listed as a control entry. Important for the state of the controversy: the same experimental signature - a long-lived second harmonic after a THz pulse - that is read elsewhere as light-induced ferroelectricity is here traced explicitly back to defect physics. The fluence-dependent hardening of the soft mode can be described by a single-well potential, so no ferroelectric double well arises.
